newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ex-Moscow air cargo mkt very busy, but rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Moscow air cargo mkt very busy, but rates steady.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport were generally steady in the last three weeks, but market was very active, forwarders said.
Peter Vins, president of Vinlund Air, told Reuters that his company had many shipments during first ten days of December. "The market is a very active," he said.
David Stone, managing director of Cargo international Services, said the market was quite busy. But next two weeks it was likely to calm down due to holidays, he said.
"Air cargo rates showed practically did not change," Stone said.

Lilia Sirbu, managing director of Icaros International Cargo Service, said import cargo operations were more profitable than export cargo operations. "95 per cent of our activity is import and only five per cent are export cargos," she said.
Rates to Luxemburg from Russia's leading air cargo gateway fell one cent to $1.30 per kg for a 100 kg shipment.
Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow said market activity will be grow before December 30 and in the second fortnight of January.
"We will have a little two-week rest in the beginning of the year and then market will become active again," he said.

Nikolai Belyaev, sales manager of EMS Garant Post, which is a forwarder for Air France said cargo turnovers may grow two fold before Christmas. "Many clients rush to carry out their contracts. After the New Year holiday we also hope a strong market until May," he added.
Ben Scott, Federal Express marketing director for Central and Eastern Europe, said the air cargo market in Russia was becoming more and more competitive.
"UPS ), DHL, and TNT are working here now and we feel the market as a very dinamic," he said.
"We have many shipments these days," Scott said, adding that 80 per cent of FedEx customers in Russia are companies and 20 per cent individuals.
Sirbu said the market ignored the impact of a 10 cent fuel surcharge imposed by foreign airlines. "Russian carriers do not rush to increase their rates or impose fuel surcharge," she said.
She said her company expected many new orders for next year to carry import medicines. "We see 100 per cent growing of these deliveries."
Meanwhile, rates to two key South East Asia destinations -- Seul and Tokyo -- fell two cents to $4.00 and $4.17 respectively.

A sales manager for Aeroservice forwarder firm said in the last three weeks her company had a strong export shipments to South East Asia. "We hope it will be more active during next two weeks," said the manager who refused to be indentified.
A senior manager of Chapman Freeborn Russia said that there were good transit shipments from Western Europe to Siberia via Moscow. "This direction is promising," she added.
Forwarders are optimistic about their operations on Russian domestic cargo routes because demand is growing there.
Vins said his company planned to set up agents network in Russia. "About 60 agents will start work from the new year in the regions where our main clients have their officies," he said.
Vins also said that more clients preferred to carry their cargos to Russian regions without transit stopover in Moscow because of complicated customs clearence procedures.
"I see as very promising the Volga River region, the Urals, eastern Siberia and southern Russia," he said.
Mordvinov said Burlington Air Express Moscow would begin to operate on the new cargo route between Moscow and Tunis from the begining of next year.
He also said routes to Argentina and Chile would be busy with deliveries of spare parts for tractors and cars from Russia.
"Russia-Peru cargo flights may be more active next year, after Peru goverment had decided to pay Russia the $162 million debt," Mordvinov added.

Scott said FedEx was looking for future interline agreements with Aeroflot and Transaero to expand delivering of cargo in several Russian and CIS destinations. "St Petersburg has priority in our plans," Scott said.
Sirbu said that some clients are switching back to air cargo deliveries to Russia after they had faced problems with customs when delivering cargos by trucks.
She said her company hopes to get a big order from Germany's Siemens group to carry its equipment by air from Western Europe to Siberia from the begining of next year.
